title: El pleito
goal: Get between two neighbours arguing over a wall
culture: A shouting match on the street is public and everybody watches, which is also what settles it: nobody wants to be the one who would not calm down. A third person saying no es para tanto is a recognised role, and it is not interfering.

beats.es: ¡Esa pared es mía! ¡Yo la levanté con mi plata!
beats.good: Cálmese, usted, and with vecino after it. The word alone can sound like an order; with vecino it is somebody on his side.

beats.es: ¡Es que me corrió la cerca! ¡Medio metro me quitó!
beats.objective: Say it is not that big a thing
beats.en: It’s not such a big deal, man.
beats.good: No es para tanto shrinks it, and shrinking it is the entire job. You are not judging who is right and nobody has asked you to.

beats.es: ¡Es que usted no sabe! ¡Toda la vida hemos vivido aquí!
beats.objective: Say it can be talked out
beats.en: It can be sorted out by talking, neighbour.
beats.good: Hablando se arregla — talking sorts it out. It is a proverb and it works because it hands both of them a way to stop without losing.

beats.es: ...Bueno. Bueno pues. Que venga y hablamos.
beats.good: Ya estuvo ends it: that is enough, it is over, done. Said at the right moment it lets everybody walk away having agreed to stop rather than having given in.
